title.zh: 卷一百十四 列傳第五十二: 白華 斜卯愛實附:合周 石抹世勣
title.en: Volume 114 Biographies 52: Bai Hua, Xiemaoaishi relative: Hezhou, Shimoshiji
title.raw: 卷一百十四 列傳第五十二: 白華 斜卯愛實附:合周 石抹世勣 Volume 114 Biographies 52: Bai Hua, Xiemaoaishi relative: Hezhou, Shimoshiji

sentences.zh: 三年五月，宋人掠壽州，永州桃園軍失利，死者四百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Song forces raided Shou Prefecture; the Taoyuan Army of Yong Prefecture was defeated, with more than four hundred dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, the Song raided Shou Prefecture, and the Taoyuan Army at Yong Prefecture was defeated, leaving more than four hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 時夏全自楚州來奔。

translations.literal: At that time Xia Quan came from Chu Prefecture to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xia Quan defected from Chu Prefecture and came over to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚申，集百官議和宋。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen in the eleventh month, all officials were assembled to discuss peace with the Song.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the eleventh month, the court gathered the officials to deliberate on making peace with the Song.

sentences.zh: 上問全所以來，華奏：「全初在盱眙，從宋帥劉卓往楚州。

translations.literal: The emperor asked why Quan had come; Hua memorialized: "Quan was at first at Xuyi, following the Song commander Liu Zhuo to Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why Quan had come, Hua reported: "Quan had been at Xuyi and followed the Song commander Liu Zhuo to Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人訛言劉大帥來，欲屠城中北人耳。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture spread a false rumor that Grand Commander Liu was coming to massacre all the northerners in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople spread a rumor that Grand Commander Liu was coming to slaughter every northerner in the city.

sentences.zh: 眾軍怒，殺卓以城來歸。

translations.literal: The troops were enraged, killed Zhuo, and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers, enraged, killed Zhuo and offered the city in surrender.

sentences.zh: 全終不自安，跳走盱眙，盱眙不納，城下索妻孥，又不從，計無所出，乃狼狽而北，止求自免，無他慮也。」

translations.literal: Quan was never at ease in the end; he fled to Xuyi, but Xuyi would not admit him; below the walls he demanded his wife and children, and they would not comply; with no plan left, he fled north in disarray, seeking only to save himself, with no other design."
translations.idiomatic: Quan never felt secure; he bolted to Xuyi, which refused him entry, then stood below the walls demanding his wife and children, which was also refused. With nowhere to turn, he fled north in disorder, asking only to save his own skin and nothing more."

sentences.zh: 華因是為上所知。

translations.literal: Through this Hua came to be known by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Hua won the emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 全至後，盱眙、楚州，王義深、張惠、范成進相繼以城降。

translations.literal: After Quan arrived, Xuyi and Chu Prefecture, Wang Yishen, Zhang Hui, and Fan Chengjin surrendered their cities in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Quan arrived, Wang Yishen, Zhang Hui, and Fan Chengjin surrendered Xuyi and Chu Prefecture one after another.

sentences.zh: 詔改楚州為平淮府，以全為金源郡王、平淮府都總管，張惠臨淄郡王，義深東平郡王，成進膠西郡王。

translations.literal: An edict changed Chu Prefecture to Pinghuai Prefecture, appointing Quan as Prince of Jinyuan and chief commander of Pinghuai Prefecture, Zhang Hui as Prince of Linzi, Yishen as Prince of Dongping, and Chengjin as Prince of Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Chu Prefecture Pinghuai Prefecture, made Quan Prince of Jinyuan and chief commander of Pinghuai, Zhang Hui Prince of Linzi, Yishen Prince of Dongping, and Chengjin Prince of Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 和宋議寢。

translations.literal: The deliberations on peace with the Song were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Talk of peace with the Song was set aside.

sentences.zh: 四年，李全據楚州，眾皆謂盱眙不可守，上不從，乃以淮南王招全，全曰：「王義深、范成進皆我部曲而受王封，何以處我。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year Li Quan held Chu Prefecture; everyone said Xuyi could not be held, but the emperor would not agree; he then enfeoffed Quan as Prince of Huainan, but Quan said: "Wang Yishen and Fan Chengjin were both my subordinates yet received princely titles—how will you treat me?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Li Quan held Chu Prefecture. Many said Xuyi could not be defended, but the emperor refused to abandon it and enfeoffed Quan as Prince of Huainan. Quan replied: "Yishen and Chengjin were my own men yet were made princes—what rank do you intend for me?"

sentences.zh: 竟不至。

translations.literal: In the end he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He never came.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慶山奴敗績於龜山。

translations.literal: That year Qingshan Nu was defeated at Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qingshan Nu suffered defeat at Guishan.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，增築歸德城，擬工數百萬，宰相奏遣華往相役，華見行院溫撒辛，語以民勞，朝廷愛養之意，減工三之一。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, the walls of Guide were enlarged, with projected labor in the millions; the chief ministers memorialized sending Hua to oversee the corvée; Hua saw Wensa Xin of the Directorate and spoke of the people's toil and the court's wish to cherish them, reducing the labor by one third.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year the enlargement of Guide's walls was projected to cost millions in labor; the chief ministers proposed sending Hua to supervise the work. Hua met Wensa Xin of the Directorate, spoke of the people's exhaustion and the court's care for them, and cut the labor by a third.

sentences.zh: 溫撒，李辛賜姓也。

translations.literal: Wensa was Li Xin, to whom a surname had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wensa was Li Xin, who had been granted a surname.

sentences.zh: 六年，以華權樞密院判官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hua was made acting judge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hua was appointed acting judge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上召忠孝軍總領蒲察定住、經歷王仲澤、戶部郎中刁璧及華諭之曰：「李全據有楚州，睥睨山東，久必為患。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief of the Loyal and Filial Army Pucha Dingzhu, the staff officer Wang Zhongze, the bureau director Dia Bi, and Hua and instructed them: "Li Quan holds Chu Prefecture and looks covetously toward Shandong; in time he will surely become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Pucha Dingzhu, chief of the Loyal and Filial Army, Wang Zhongze, staff officer, Dia Bi of the Revenue Bureau, and Hua and said: "Li Quan holds Chu Prefecture and eyes Shandong; before long he will be a menace.

sentences.zh: 今北事稍緩，合乘此隙令定住權監軍，率所統軍一千，別遣都尉司步軍萬人，以璧、仲澤為參謀，同往沂、海界招之，不從則以軍馬從事，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: Now that affairs in the north have eased somewhat, we should seize this interval and have Dingzhu act as provisional overseer of the army, leading the thousand men under his command, while separately dispatching the infantry of the Cavalry Command with ten thousand men, with Bi and Zhongze as staff officers, to go to the Yi and Hai frontier to summon him; if he does not comply, then take military action—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The northern front has slackened; use this opening to let Dingzhu oversee the army in the field with his thousand men, send ten thousand infantry of the Cavalry Command, and send Bi and Zhongze as advisers to summon Quan on the Yi–Hai border. If he refuses, move against him with horse and foot. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 華對曰：「臣以為李全借大兵之勢，要宋人供給饋餉，特一猾寇耳。

translations.literal: Hua replied: "Your servant thinks Li Quan relies on the might of a great army to demand that the Song supply him with provisions—he is only a cunning bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Hua answered: "I believe Li Quan leans on our great army's strength to force the Song to feed him—nothing but a slippery outlaw.

sentences.zh: 老狐穴塚，待夜而出，何足介懷。

translations.literal: An old fox in its den waits for night to come out—why should we care?
translations.idiomatic: An old fox in its burrow waits for night to stir—why trouble ourselves?

sentences.zh: 我所慮者北方之強耳。

translations.literal: What I worry about is the strength of the north.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles me is the power to the north.

sentences.zh: 今北方有事，未暇南圖，一旦事定，必來攻矣。

translations.literal: Now the north has its own affairs and has no leisure to look south; once those affairs are settled, they will surely come to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The northern power is occupied elsewhere and has no time to turn south; when that business is done, they will attack us.

sentences.zh: 與我爭天下者此也，全何預焉。

translations.literal: It is they who will contend with us for the realm; what has Quan to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: They are the ones who will fight us for the empire—what is Quan to that?

sentences.zh: 若北方事定，全將聽命不暇，設不自量，更有非望，天下之人寧不知逆順，其肯去順而從逆乎！

translations.literal: If the northern affairs are settled, Quan will have no time even to obey orders; should he overreach himself with further ambitions, would the people of the realm not know right from wrong—who would leave the righteous to follow the rebel?
translations.idiomatic: When the north is settled, Quan will barely keep pace with our orders; if he dares more, will anyone under heaven not know loyalty from treason—who would abandon the lawful to follow a rebel?

sentences.zh: 為今計者，姑養士馬，以備北方。

translations.literal: For the present plan, let us for the moment nurture soldiers and horses to prepare against the north.
translations.idiomatic: The policy for now is to rest soldiers and horses against the northern threat.

sentences.zh: 使全果有不軌之謀，亦當發於北朝息兵之日，當此則我易與矣。」

translations.literal: If Quan should indeed harbor disloyal designs, they will emerge only when the northern dynasty has ceased fighting; at that time we can deal with him easily."
translations.idiomatic: Any treason in Quan will show itself only after the northern dynasty stands down; then he will be easy to handle."

sentences.zh: 上沉思良久曰：「卿等且退，容我更思。」

translations.literal: The emperor pondered a long while and said: "You may withdraw for now; let me think further."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought long and said: "Withdraw for now; I must consider further."

sentences.zh: 明日，遣定住還屯尉氏。

translations.literal: The next day he sent Dingzhu back to garrison Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered Dingzhu back to camp at Weishi.

sentences.zh: 時陝西兵大勢已去，留脫或欒駐慶陽以擾河朔，且有攻河中之耗，而衛州帥府與恆山公府並立，慮一旦有警，節制不一，欲合二府為一，又恐其不和，命華往經畫之。

translations.literal: At that time the great strength of the Shaanxi army had already departed; Tuo Wo or Luan remained at Qingyang to harass the Hebei region, and there were also reports of an attack on the Middle He region; meanwhile the command at Weizhou and the office of the Duke of Hengshan stood side by side, and fearing that if an emergency arose command would not be unified, they wished to merge the two offices into one, yet feared they would not get along, and ordered Hua to go and arrange matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi army's main force was already gone; Tuo Wo or Luan held Qingyang to trouble Hebei, with word of a thrust at the Middle He. The Weizhou command and the Duke of Hengshan's office both stood, and lest an alarm find them divided, the court wished to unite them but feared discord, and sent Hua to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 初，華在院屢承面諭云：「汝為院官，不以軍馬責汝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hua was in the bureau he had repeatedly received face-to-face instructions: "You are a bureau official; I do not hold you responsible for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before, while Hua served in the bureau, the emperor had told him repeatedly: "As a bureau officer I do not charge you with armies.

sentences.zh: 汝辭辯，特以合喜、蒲阿皆武夫，一語不相入，便為齟齬，害事非細，今以汝調停之，或有乖忤，罪及汝矣。

translations.literal: You are eloquent; it is only that Hexi and Pu A are both warriors—if one word does not agree, friction arises, and harm to affairs is no small matter; now I send you to mediate; if there is any clash, the blame falls on you.
translations.idiomatic: You are quick with words; Hexi and Pu A are soldiers, and a single disagreement breeds friction that harms the state. I send you to mediate—any breach, and you bear it.

sentences.zh: 院中事當一一奏我，汝之職也。

translations.literal: Bureau affairs should each be reported to me—that is your duty.
translations.idiomatic: Report every bureau matter to me—that is your charge.

sentences.zh: 今衛州之委，亦前日調停之意。」

translations.literal: The commission at Weizhou is likewise in the spirit of that earlier mediation."
translations.idiomatic: The Weizhou assignment is the same kind of mediation."

sentences.zh: 國制，凡樞密院上下所倚任者名奏事官，其目有三，一曰承受聖旨，二曰奏事，三曰省院議事，皆以一人主之。

translations.literal: Under the state system, those in the Bureau of Military Affairs on whom superiors and subordinates relied were called memorial officers; there were three categories: receiving the sacred edict, memorializing, and deliberating with the provincial offices—all entrusted to one man.
translations.idiomatic: By state rule, the men the Bureau of Military Affairs relied on were called memorial officers, in three kinds: receiving the sacred edict, memorializing, and deliberating with the provincial offices—each held by one person.

sentences.zh: 承受聖旨者，凡院官奏事，或上處分，獨召奏事官付之，多至一二百言，或直傳上旨，辭多者即與近侍局官批寫。

translations.literal: The receiver of sacred edicts: whenever a bureau officer memorialized, or the emperor issued a disposition, or the memorial officer alone was summoned, the charge was given to him, often up to one or two hundred words, or the emperor's intent was transmitted directly; if the wording was long, it was drafted with an officer of the Inner Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The receiver of edicts took every bureau memorial, imperial disposition, or private summons, often one or two hundred words, or the emperor's words directly; longer orders were drafted with the Inner Service Bureau.

sentences.zh: 奏事者，謂事有區處當取奏裁者殿奏，其奏每嫌辭費，必欲言簡而意明，退而奉行，即立文字，謂之檢目。

translations.literal: The memorializer: matters requiring disposition and imperial decision were presented in audience; the memorials were thought too wordy, and brevity with clear intent was required; on withdrawal they were executed and written up, called inspection items.
translations.idiomatic: The memorializer presented matters needing the throne's ruling; memorials had to be brief and clear, then on withdrawal were executed as written inspection items.

sentences.zh: 省院官殿上議事則默記之，議定歸院，亦立檢目呈覆。

translations.literal: When provincial officers deliberated in the hall, he recorded silently; when deliberation was settled they returned to the bureau and likewise drew up inspection items for submission.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial officers debated in court he noted in silence; when debate ended they returned to the bureau and submitted inspection items.

sentences.zh: 有疑則復稟，無則付掾史施行。

translations.literal: If there was doubt they reported again; if not, they handed it to the clerks for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Doubts were reported again; otherwise clerks carried them out.

sentences.zh: 其赴省議者，議既定，留奏事官與省左右司官同立奏草，圓覆諸相無異同，則右司奏上。

translations.literal: Those who went to the provincial offices to deliberate: when deliberation was fixed, the memorial officer stayed with the left and right officers of the province to draft the memorial together; if all ministers agreed without difference, the right officer presented it.
translations.idiomatic: For provincial deliberation, once settled the memorial officer and the province's left and right officers drafted the memorial; if all ministers agreed, the right officer submitted it.

sentences.zh: 此三者之外又有難者，曰備顧問，如軍馬糧草器械、軍帥部曲名數、與夫屯駐地裏厄塞遠近之類，凡省院一切事務，顧問之際一不能應，輒以不用心被譴，其職為甚難，故以華處之。

translations.literal: Beyond these three there was another, harder post: adviser on call—such as horses, grain, weapons, commanders' rosters, and the geography of encampments, passes, and distances—for any bureau or provincial affair, if at consultation he could not answer once, he was rebuked for inattention; the duty was very hard, and therefore Hua was placed in it.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these was the harder role of adviser on call—horses, grain, arms, commanders' rolls, camp terrain, passes, distances—for any bureau or provincial matter, one failure at consultation brought rebuke; the post was arduous, and Hua was given it.

sentences.zh: 五月，以丞相賽不行尚書省事于關中，蒲阿率完顏陳和尚忠孝軍一千駐邠州，且令審觀北勢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the chief minister Sai was unable to attend to Ministry of Revenue affairs in Guanzhong; Pu A led a thousand of the Loyal and Filial Army under Wanyan Chenheshang to garrison Bin Prefecture and observe the northern situation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Chief Minister Sai could not manage Revenue affairs in Guanzhong; Pu A led a thousand Loyal and Filial troops under Wanyan Chenheshang to Bin Prefecture to watch the north.

sentences.zh: 如是兩月，上謂白華曰：「汝往邠州六日可往復否？」

translations.literal: After two months thus, the emperor said to Bai Hua: "Can you go to Bin Prefecture and return within six days?"
translations.idiomatic: After two months the emperor asked Bai Hua: "Can you reach Bin and return in six days?"

sentences.zh: 華自量日可馳三百，應之曰：「可。」

translations.literal: Hua estimated he could ride three hundred li a day and answered: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Hua reckoned three hundred li a day and said: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 上令密諭蒲阿才候春首，當事慶陽。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to tell Pu A secretly to wait until the turn of spring, then act at Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to instruct Pu A in secret to wait for early spring, then strike at Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 華如期而還。

translations.literal: Hua returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Hua returned on time.

sentences.zh: 上一日顧謂華言：「我見汝從來凡語及征進，必有難色，今此一舉特銳于平時，何也？」

translations.literal: One day the emperor remarked to Hua: "Whenever you speak of campaigning, you always look troubled; this time you are sharper than usual—why?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor said to Hua: "Whenever we speak of campaigning you look uneasy; this time you are keener than usual—why?"

sentences.zh: 華曰：「向日用兵，以南征及討李全之事梗之，不能專意北方，故以北向為難。

translations.literal: Hua said: "In former days military use was blocked by the southern campaigns and the operations against Li Quan, so we could not focus on the north; hence campaigning northward was hard.
translations.idiomatic: Hua said: "Before, southern wars and the Li Quan affair blocked us from facing north, so a northern campaign was hard.

sentences.zh: 今日異于平時，況事至於此，不得不一舉。

translations.literal: Today is unlike ordinary times; moreover affairs have come to this pass—we must strike once.
translations.idiomatic: Now is not ordinary times, and matters have reached this point—we must act.

sentences.zh: 大軍入界已三百餘里，若縱之令下秦川則何以救，終當一戰摧之。

translations.literal: The great army has already penetrated more than three hundred li; if we let them descend into the Qin plain, how can we save it—we must finally fight once and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Their main force is three hundred li in; if we let them down into the Qin plain there is no saving it—we must fight and crush them.

sentences.zh: 戰于近裏之平川，不若戰于近邊之險隘。」

translations.literal: Better to fight in the narrow passes near the frontier than on the open plains nearby."
translations.idiomatic: Battle in frontier narrows, not on nearby open ground.

sentences.zh: 上亦以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor also thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，慶陽圍解，大軍還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year the siege of Qingyang was lifted and the great army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Qingyang's siege was raised and the great army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 白華上奏：「凡今之計，兵食為急。

translations.literal: Bai Hua memorialized: "For every plan today, troops and food are urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Hua memorialized: "Every policy today turns on troops and grain.

sentences.zh: 除密院已定忠孝軍及馬軍都尉司步軍足為一戰之資，此外應河南府州亦須簽揀防城軍，秋聚春放，依古務農講武之義，各令防本州府城，以今見在九十七萬，無致他日為資敵之用。」

translations.literal: Apart from the Loyal and Filial Army and the cavalry and infantry of the Command already fixed by the secret bureau as enough for one battle, the prefectures south of the river should also muster garrison troops, gathered in autumn and released in spring, in the ancient spirit of farming in season and drilling in season, each to defend its prefectural seat, with the present ninety-seven thousand, lest they one day feed the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Besides the Loyal and Filial Army and the cavalry and infantry command already set by the secret bureau for one battle, southern prefectures should muster garrison troops—mustered in autumn, released in spring—in the old way of farming and drilling, each to hold its city, keeping the present ninety-seven thousand from ever arming the foe.

sentences.zh: 五月，華真授樞密判官，上遣近侍局副使七斤傳旨云：「朕用汝為院官，非責汝將兵對壘，第欲汝立軍中綱紀、發遣文移、和睦將帥、究察非違，至於軍伍之閱習、器仗之修整，皆汝所職。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Hua was fully appointed judge of the secret bureau; the emperor sent the deputy of the Inner Service Bureau Qijin to transmit the edict: "I use you as a bureau officer, not to hold the line against the enemy in person, but to set military discipline, issue documents, harmonize commanders, and investigate violations; as for drilling troops and repairing weapons, all are your charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Hua received full appointment as bureau judge; the emperor sent Inner Service deputy Qijin with the edict: "I made you a bureau officer not to duel the enemy in the field, but to enforce discipline, dispatch papers, reconcile commanders, and probe misconduct; drilling troops and repairing arms are yours.

sentences.zh: 其悉力國家，以稱朕意。」

translations.literal: Devote your strength to the state to match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Serve the state with all your strength, as I expect."

sentences.zh: 八年，大軍自去歲入陝西，翱翔京兆、同、華之間，破南山砦柵六十餘所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the great army, having entered Shaanxi the year before, ranged between Jingzhao and Tong and Hua, and broke more than sixty stockades in the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the army that had entered Shaanxi the year before ranged between Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua and stormed more than sixty southern mountain stockades.

sentences.zh: 已而攻鳳翔，金軍自閿鄉屯至澠池，兩行省晏然不動。

translations.literal: Soon they attacked Fengxiang; Jin troops moved from Min to Mianchi, while the two provincial offices sat unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Fengxiang; Jin forces moved from Min to Mianchi while both provincial offices did nothing.

sentences.zh: 宰相台諫皆以樞院瞻望逗遛為言，京兆士庶橫議蜂起，以至諸相力奏上前。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and remonstrance officials all said the secret bureau was watching and delaying; the people of Jingzhao gossiped wildly, until the ministers pressed the emperor in force.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and censors accused the secret bureau of delay; Jingzhao murmured until every minister pressed the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「合達、蒲阿必相度機會，可進而進耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Heda and Pu A must gauge the moment and advance when they can.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Heda and Pu A will seize the moment and advance when they may.

sentences.zh: 若督之使戰，終出勉強，恐無益而反害也。」

translations.literal: If we press them to fight, in the end it will be forced, and I fear it will harm rather than help."
translations.idiomatic: Force them to battle and it will be reluctant—I fear harm, not help.

sentences.zh: 因遣白華與右司郎中夾谷八里門道宰相百官所言，並問以「目今二月過半，有怠歸之形，諸軍何故不動？」

translations.literal: He therefore sent Bai Hua with the right bureau director Jiagu Balimen to tell the chief ministers what the officials had said, and also to ask: "It is now more than half of the second month, and they show signs of slackening their return—why do the armies not move?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bai Hua with right bureau director Jiagu Balimen to relay the ministers' words and ask: "Half of the second month is past and they seem ready to withdraw—why do the armies not move?"

sentences.zh: 且詔華等往復六日。

translations.literal: He also ordered Hua and the others to return within six days.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Hua six days for the round trip.

sentences.zh: 華等既到同，諭兩行省以上意。

translations.literal: When Hua and the others reached Tong, they conveyed the emperor's intent to both provincial offices.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong, Hua and his party delivered the emperor's message to both provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 合達言：「不見機會，見則動耳。」

translations.literal: Heda said: "Without seeing the opportunity, one does not move; when one sees it, one moves."
translations.idiomatic: Heda said: "Without an opening we do not move; when we see one, we do."

sentences.zh: 蒲阿曰：「彼軍絕無糧餉，使欲戰不得，欲留不能，將自敝矣。」

translations.literal: Pu A said: "Their army has absolutely no grain; even if they wished to fight they could not, even if they wished to stay they could not—they will wear themselves out."
translations.idiomatic: Pu A said: "They have no grain at all; they cannot fight if they wish, nor stay if they wish—they will exhaust themselves."

sentences.zh: 合達對蒲阿及諸帥則言不可動，見士大夫則言可動，人謂合達近嘗得罪，又畏蒲阿方得君，不敢與抗，而亦言不可動。

translations.literal: Heda told Pu A and the commanders that they must not move, but told the scholar-officials they could move; people said Heda had recently offended and feared Pu A's favor with the emperor, dared not resist, and therefore also said they must not move.
translations.idiomatic: To Pu A and the generals Heda said they must not move; to the literati he said they could. Men said Heda had lately given offense and, fearing Pu A's favor, dared not oppose him and so also said no move.

sentences.zh: 華等觀二相見北兵勢大皆有懼心，遂私問樊澤、定住、陳和尚以為何如，三人者皆曰：」他人言北兵疲困，故可攻，此言非也。

translations.literal: Hua and the others saw both chief ministers feared the northern army's strength; they privately asked Fan Ze, Dingzhu, and Chenheshang what they thought; all three said: "Others say the northern army is weary and can be attacked—that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hua saw both ministers feared the northern host and privately asked Fan Ze, Dingzhu, and Chenheshang; all three said: "The talk that the northern army is spent and can be attacked is wrong.

sentences.zh: 大兵所在，豈可輕料？

translations.literal: Wherever the great army is, how can one lightly estimate it?
translations.idiomatic: How can one lightly judge where the main army stands?

sentences.zh: 是真不敢動。」

translations.literal: They truly dare not move."
translations.idiomatic: They truly dare not move.

sentences.zh: 華等還，以二相及諸將意奏之，上曰：」我故知其怯不敢動矣。」

translations.literal: When Hua and the others returned and reported the two chief ministers' and the generals' views, the emperor said: "I knew already they were timid and dared not move."
translations.idiomatic: Hua reported the ministers' and generals' views; the emperor said: "I knew they were too timid to move."

sentences.zh: 即復遣華傳旨諭二相云：「鳳翔圍久，恐守者力不能支。

translations.literal: He immediately sent Hua again to instruct the two chief ministers: "The siege of Fengxiang has been long; I fear the defenders' strength cannot hold.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hua again to tell both ministers: "Fengxiang has been besieged long; the defenders may not hold.

sentences.zh: 行省當領軍出關，宿華陰界，次日及華陰，次日及華州，略與渭北軍交手。

translations.literal: The provincial office should lead the army out of the pass and camp on the Huayin border; the next day reach Huayin, the next day reach Hua Prefecture, and briefly engage the Weibei army.
translations.idiomatic: Lead the army out of the pass, camp on the Huayin frontier, reach Huayin the next day and Hua Prefecture the day after, and skirmish with the Weibei force.

sentences.zh: 計大兵聞之必當奔赴，且以少紓鳳翔之急，我亦得為掣肘計耳。」

translations.literal: I reckon the great army, hearing this, will surely hurry over, and it will somewhat ease Fengxiang's peril; we shall also gain a means of pulling them back."
translations.idiomatic: The main army will hurry over, easing Fengxiang a little and giving us a lever.

sentences.zh: 二相回奏領旨。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers memorialized in reply that they had received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Both ministers memorialized receipt of the order.

sentences.zh: 華東還及中牟，已有兩行省納奏人追及，華取報密院副本讀之，言：「領旨提軍出關二十里至華陰界，與渭北軍交，是晚收軍入關。」

translations.literal: Hua was returning east and had reached Zhongmou when messengers from both provincial offices overtook him; Hua read a copy of the secret bureau report: "Having received the edict we led the army out of the pass twenty li to the Huayin border, engaged the Weibei army, and that evening withdrew into the pass."
translations.idiomatic: Hua was east of Zhongmou when provincial messengers caught him; he read the bureau copy: "We led the army twenty li beyond the pass to Huayin, fought the Weibei force, and withdrew into the pass that evening.

sentences.zh: 華為之仰天浩歎曰：「事至於此，無如之何矣。」

translations.literal: Hua looked up to heaven and sighed greatly: "Affairs have come to this—nothing can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Hua sighed to heaven: "It has come to this—nothing can be done."

sentences.zh: 華至京，奏章已達，知所奏為徒然，不二三日鳳翔陷，兩行省遂棄京兆，與牙古塔起遷居民于河南，留慶山奴守之。

translations.literal: When Hua reached the capital his memorial had already arrived; he knew what he had reported was in vain; within two or three days Fengxiang fell, both provincial offices abandoned Jingzhao, and with Yaguta they moved the inhabitants to Henan, leaving Qingshan Nu to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital his memorial was already in; he knew it was useless. In two or three days Fengxiang fell; both offices abandoned Jingzhao, moved the people to Henan with Yaguta, and left Qingshan Nu behind.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，楊妙真以夫李全死于宋，構浮橋于楚州之北，就北帥梭魯胡吐乞師復仇。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Yang Miaozhen, because her husband Li Quan had died at the hands of the Song, built a pontoon bridge north of Chu Prefecture and asked the northern commander Soluhutu for troops to avenge him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Yang Miaozhen—her husband Li Quan having been killed by the Song—built a pontoon bridge north of Chu Prefecture and asked the northern commander Soluhutu for troops to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷覘知之，以謂北軍果能渡淮，淮與河南跬步間耳，遣合達、蒲阿駐軍桃源界滶河口備之。

translations.literal: The court learned of it and judged that if the northern army could truly cross the Huai, the Huai and Henan were but a step apart; they sent Heda and Pu A to garrison at the Taoyuan frontier at the Mo River mouth to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of it and judged that if the northern army crossed the Huai, Henan lay a step away; Heda and Pu A were sent to the Taoyuan frontier at the Mo River mouth.

sentences.zh: 兩行省乃約宋帥趙范，趙葵為夾攻之計。

translations.literal: The two provincial offices then agreed with the Song commanders Zhao Fan and Zhao Kui on a plan of joint attack.
translations.idiomatic: Both provincial offices then arranged with Song commanders Zhao Fan and Zhao Kui for a joint attack.

sentences.zh: 二趙亦遣人報聘，俱以議和為名，以張聲勢。

translations.literal: The two Zhaos also sent envoys with courtesies, both in the name of discussing peace, to magnify their presence.
translations.idiomatic: The two Zhaos sent envoys as well, all under the name of peace talks, to swell their show of force.

sentences.zh: 二相屢以軍少為言，而省院難之，因上奏云：「向來附關屯駐半年，適還舊屯，喘不及息，又欲以暑月東行，實無可圖之事，徒自疲而已。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers repeatedly pleaded scant troops, while the provincial and bureau offices resisted; they therefore memorialized: "Previously we camped at Fu Pass for half a year and had only just returned to the old camps, scarcely catching our breath, and now they wish us to march east in the heat of summer—there is truly nothing to gain, only exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The two ministers pleaded few troops while the provincial and bureau offices objected; they memorialized: "We camped at Fu Pass half a year and have only just returned, scarcely breathing, and now they want us east in summer heat—there is nothing to gain, only weariness.

sentences.zh: 況兼桃源、青口蚊虻湫濕之地，不便牧養，目今非征進時月，決不敢妄動。

translations.literal: Moreover Taoyuan and Qingkou are muggy, fly-ridden marshes, ill for grazing; this is not the season for campaigning, and we dare not move rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Taoyuan and Qingkou are fly-ridden marshes, poor for grazing; this is not the season to campaign, and we dare not stir rashly.

sentences.zh: 且我之所慮，特楚州浮梁耳。

translations.literal: What we worry about is only the pontoon bridge at Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: We worry only about the pontoon at Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姑以計圖之，已遣提控王銳往視可否。」

translations.literal: For the moment let us scheme against it; we have already sent the commander Wang Rui to see whether it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: For now let us plot against it; we have sent Commander Wang Rui to see if it is feasible.

sentences.zh: 奏上，上遣白華以此傳諭二相，兼領王銳行。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor sent Bai Hua to convey this to the two chief ministers and also to lead Wang Rui's mission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Bai Hua to tell both ministers and to accompany Wang Rui.

sentences.zh: 二相不悅。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Both ministers were displeased.

sentences.zh: 蒲阿遣水軍虹縣所屯王提控者以小船二十四隻，令華順河而下，必到八里莊城門為期，且曰：「此中望八里莊，如在雲間天上，省院端坐，徒事口吻，今樞判親來，可以相視可否，歸而奏之。」

translations.literal: Pu A sent the naval commander Wang at the Hong county station with twenty-four small boats, ordering Hua to go downriver and reach the gate of Balizhuang city by a set time, and said: "From here Balizhuang looks as if it were in the clouds and sky; the provincial and bureau offices sit idle, wagging tongues only; now the bureau judge comes in person—you can see for yourselves whether it is feasible and report on your return."
translations.idiomatic: Pu A sent the naval commander Wang at Hong county with twenty-four small boats and ordered Hua downriver to reach Balizhuang's gate on schedule, saying: "From here Balizhuang seems in the clouds; the capital offices sit and talk; now the bureau judge comes—you can see for yourselves and report back.

sentences.zh: 華力辭不獲，遂登舟。

translations.literal: Hua strove to decline but could not, and boarded the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Hua protested in vain and boarded.

sentences.zh: 及淮與河合流處，才及八里莊城門相直，城守者以白鷂大船五十溯流而上，占其上流以截華歸路。

translations.literal: Where the Huai and the river joined, he had only come opposite the gate of Balizhuang when the defenders sent fifty large white-hawk boats upstream to seize the upper stream and cut off Hua's return.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai–river confluence he had only lined up with Balizhuang's gate when the garrison sent fifty large "white hawk" boats upstream to block his return.

sentences.zh: 華幾不得還，昏黑得徑先歸，乃悟兩省怒朝省不益軍，謂皆華輩主之，故擠之險地耳。

translations.literal: Hua nearly could not return; in the dark he found a shortcut and got back first, and then understood that both provincial offices were angry that the capital would not increase troops, thinking it was all managed by men like Hua, and had squeezed him into danger.
translations.idiomatic: Hua nearly failed to return; in the dark he took a bypath and got back first, and understood both offices were angry the capital would not add troops, blamed men like Hua, and had pushed him into peril.

sentences.zh: 是夜二更後，八里莊次將遣人送款云：「早者主將出城開船，截大金歸路，某等商議，主將還即閉門不納，渠已奔去楚州，乞發軍馬接應。」

translations.literal: After the second watch that night the deputy at Balizhuang sent word of surrender: "Earlier the commander went out to open boats and cut off the Great Jin's return route; we discussed among ourselves and when the commander returned we would not admit him; he has already fled to Chu Prefecture—please send troops to meet us."
translations.idiomatic: After the second watch Balizhuang's deputy sent surrender: "Earlier the commander went out to block the Jin return; we agreed not to admit him when he returned; he has fled to Chu Prefecture—send troops to receive us.

sentences.zh: 二相即發兵騎、開船赴約，明旦入城安慰，又知楚州大軍已還河朔，宋將燒浮橋，二相附華納奏，上大喜。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers immediately sent cavalry and opened boats to keep the appointment; at dawn they entered the city to reassure them, and also learned the great army at Chu Prefecture had returned to Hebei and Song generals had burned the pontoon bridge; the two chief ministers had Hua submit the memorial, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Both ministers sent horse and boat at once; at dawn they entered to reassure the city, learned the Chu Prefecture main force had returned to Hebei and the Song had burned the bridge; Hua submitted the memorial and the emperor rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 初，合達謀取宋淮陰。

translations.literal: Earlier Heda had planned to take Song Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Heda had planned to take Song Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 五月渡淮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 淮陰主者胡路鈐往楚州計事于楊妙真，比還，提正官郭恩送款于金，胡還不納，慟哭而去。

translations.literal: The Huaiyin commander Hu Luqian had gone to Chu Prefecture to consult Yang Miaozhen; on his return the supervising officer Guo En offered surrender to the Jin, but Hu on returning would not accept it and left weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin's commander Hu Luqian had gone to Chu to consult Yang Miaozhen; on his return Guo En, supervising officer, offered surrender to the Jin, but Hu refused and left in tears.

sentences.zh: 合達遂入淮陰，詔改歸州，以行省烏古論葉裏哥守之，郭恩為元帥右都監。

translations.literal: Heda then entered Huaiyin; an edict changed it to Gui Prefecture, with the provincial officer Wugulun Yelige as defender and Guo En as right deputy commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Heda entered Huaiyin; an edict renamed it Gui Prefecture, with provincial officer Wugulun Yelige as defender and Guo En as right deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 既而，宋人以銀絹五萬兩匹來贖盱眙龜山，宋使留館中，郭恩謀劫而取之，或報之于盱眙帥府，即以軍至，恩不果發。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Song sent fifty thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk to ransom Guishan of Xuyi; the Song envoy stayed in the guest house; Guo En plotted to seize it by force, but someone reported to the Xuyi command, which sent troops at once, and En could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Song sent fifty thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk to ransom Guishan at Xuyi; the envoy lodged at the guesthouse; Guo En plotted to seize it by force, but word reached the Xuyi command, troops came at once, and En could not act.

sentences.zh: 明日，宋將劉虎、湯孝信以船三十艘燒浮梁，因遣其將夏友諒來攻盱眙，未下。

translations.literal: The next day Song generals Liu Hu and Tang Xiaoxin with thirty boats burned the pontoon bridge and sent their general Xia Youliang to attack Xuyi, but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Liu Hu and Tang Xiaoxin of the Song burned the pontoon with thirty boats and sent Xia Youliang against Xuyi without success.

sentences.zh: 泗州總領完顏矢哥利館中銀絹，遂反。

translations.literal: The Sizhou chief Wanyan Shigel had silver and silk in the guesthouse and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou chief Wanyan Shigel had silver and silk lodged at the guesthouse and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 防禦使徒單塔剌聞變，扼罘山亭甬路，好謂之曰：「容我拜辭朝廷然後死。」

translations.literal: The defender Tushan Tala heard of the mutiny, blocked the causeway at Fushan Pavilion, and spoke kindly to him: "Allow me to bid farewell to the court and then die."
translations.idiomatic: Defender Tushan Tala, hearing the mutiny, blocked the Fushan Pavilion causeway and said kindly: "Let me take leave of the court before I die."

sentences.zh: 遂取朝服望闕拜，慟良久，投亭下水死。

translations.literal: He then put on court dress, bowed toward the palace, mourned a long while, and threw himself into the water below the pavilion to die.
translations.idiomatic: He donned court dress, bowed toward the palace, mourned long, and drowned himself in the water below the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 矢哥遂以州歸楊妙真，總帥納合買住亦以盱眙降宋。

translations.literal: Shige then surrendered the prefecture to Yang Miaozhen, and the commander-in-chief Nahan Maizhu also surrendered Xuyi to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shige surrendered the prefecture to Yang Miaozhen, and commander-in-chief Nahan Maizhu surrendered Xuyi to the Song as well.

sentences.zh: 九月，陝西行省防秋，時大兵在河中，睿宗已領兵入界，慶山奴報糧盡，將棄京兆而東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Shaanxi provincial office prepared for autumn defense; at that time the great army was in the Middle He region, Ruizong had already led troops across the border, and Qingshan Nu reported grain exhausted and intended to abandon Jingzhao and go east.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Shaanxi provincial office prepared autumn defense; the great army was in the Middle He, Ruizong had crossed the border, and Qingshan Nu reported grain spent and meant to abandon Jingzhao for the east.

sentences.zh: 一日，白華奏，偵候得睿宗所領軍馬四萬，行營軍一萬，佈置如此，「為今計者，與其就漢禦之，諸軍比到，可行半月，不若徑往河中。

translations.literal: One day Bai Hua memorialized that scouts had learned Ruizong led forty thousand horse and the camp army ten thousand, deployed thus: "For the present plan, rather than meet them in Han, by the time all armies arrive we could march half a month—better to go straight to the Middle He.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Hua memorialized that scouts reported Ruizong with forty thousand horse and ten thousand camp troops, and said: "Better than meeting them in Han after half a month's march is to strike straight for the Middle He.

sentences.zh: 目今沿河屯守，一日可渡，如此中得利，襄、漢軍馬必當遲疑不進。

translations.literal: At present the river garrisons could be crossed in a day; thus we gain the advantage in the center, and the Xiang–Han armies will surely hesitate and not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The river garrisons could be crossed in a day—we gain the center, and Xiang–Han forces will hang back.

sentences.zh: 在北為投機，在南為掣肘，臣以為如此便」。

translations.literal: In the north it is seizing opportunity; in the south it is pulling them back—I think this is expedient."
translations.idiomatic: In the north it is opportunity; in the south it is leverage—I think this best."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此策汝畫之，為得之他人？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Did you devise this plan yourself, or get it from others?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Is this your plan or someone else's?"

sentences.zh: 華曰：「臣愚見如此。」

translations.literal: Hua said: "Your servant's humble view is thus."
translations.idiomatic: Hua said: "It is my own humble view."

sentences.zh: 上平日銳于武事，聞華言若欣快者，然竟不行。

translations.literal: The emperor was usually keen on military affairs and on hearing Hua seemed pleased, yet in the end he did not act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, usually eager for war, seemed pleased at Hua's words, yet did not act.

sentences.zh: 未幾，合達自陝州進奏帖，亦為此事，上得奏甚喜。

translations.literal: Before long Heda memorialized from Shaan Prefecture on this matter as well, and the emperor was very pleased to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Heda memorialized from Shaan on the same matter, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 蒲阿時在洛陽，驛召之，蓋有意於此矣。

translations.literal: Pu A was then at Luoyang and was summoned by post—clearly the emperor had this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Pu A was at Luoyang and summoned by courier—the emperor clearly intended this.

sentences.zh: 蒲阿至，奏對之間不及此，止言大兵前鋒忒木泬統之，將出冷水穀口，且當先禦此軍。

translations.literal: When Pu A arrived, in his audience he did not touch on this, speaking only that the great army's vanguard Temu Bo commanded it and would come out Cold Water Valley, and that they should first meet this army.
translations.idiomatic: Pu A, at audience, did not mention it, saying only that vanguard Temu Bo would issue from Cold Water Valley and must be met first.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕不問此，只欲問河中可搗否。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I do not ask about that; I only wish to ask whether the Middle He can be raided."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I do not ask that—I ask whether the Middle He can be struck."

sentences.zh: 蒲阿不獲已，始言睿宗所領兵騎雖多，計皆冗雜。

translations.literal: Pu A, unable to refuse, then said that though Ruizong's horse were many, the plan was all redundant and confused.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed, Pu A said Ruizong's horse were many but the plan redundant.

sentences.zh: 大兵軍少而精，無非選鋒。

translations.literal: The great army's forces were few but elite, all picked vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The great army was few but elite—all picked vanguard.

sentences.zh: 金軍北渡，大兵必遣輜重屯於平陽之北，匿其選鋒百里之外，放我師渡，然後斷我歸路與我決戰，恐不得利。」

translations.literal: If Jin troops crossed north, the great army would surely leave baggage north of Pingyang, hide its vanguard a hundred li away, let our army cross, then cut our return and give battle—we would likely not profit.
translations.idiomatic: If we crossed north they would park baggage north of Pingyang, hide vanguard a hundred li off, let us cross, then cut our retreat and fight—we would not profit.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕料汝如此，果然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I reckoned you would say so, and indeed you have.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I reckoned you would say so—and so you have.

sentences.zh: 更不須再論，且還陝州。」

translations.literal: There is no need to discuss further; return to Shaan Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Say no more; return to Shaan."

sentences.zh: 蒲阿曰：「合達樞密使所言，此間一面革撥恐亦未盡，乞召至同議可否。」

translations.literal: Pu A said: "What Bureau Judge Heda said—on this side the reorganization may not be complete; I beg summon him to deliberate whether it is feasible."
translations.idiomatic: Pu A said: "Heda's words—reorganization here may be incomplete; summon him to judge feasibility."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「見得合達亦止此而已，往復遲滯，轉致誤事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Seeing Heda would only yield the same; going back and forth would delay and cause error."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Heda would say the same; delay would only harm affairs."

sentences.zh: 華奏合達必見機會，召至同議為便。

translations.literal: Hua memorialized that Heda would surely see the opportunity and that summoning him to deliberate together would be expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Hua said Heda would see the chance and that joint deliberation was best.

sentences.zh: 副樞赤盞合喜亦奏蒲阿、白華之言為是。

translations.literal: Deputy Bureau Judge Chisan Hexi also memorialized that Pu A and Bai Hua were right.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy judge Chisan Hexi also said Pu A and Bai Hua were right.

sentences.zh: 上乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 召合達至，上令先與密院議定，然後入見。

translations.literal: Heda was summoned; the emperor ordered him first to deliberate with the secret bureau, then enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: Heda was summoned to settle matters with the secret bureau before audience.

sentences.zh: 既議，華執合達奏帖舉似再三，竟無一先發言者。

translations.literal: After deliberation Hua held up Heda's memorial again and again, yet not one spoke first.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation Hua held up Heda's memorial repeatedly, yet no one spoke first.

sentences.zh: 移時，蒲阿言：「且勾當冷水穀一軍何如。」

translations.literal: After a while Pu A said: "For now let us deal with the Cold Water army—how about that?"
translations.idiomatic: After a while Pu A said: "Let us handle the Cold Water army first—how is that?"

sentences.zh: 合達曰：「是矣。」

translations.literal: Heda said: "That is it."
translations.idiomatic: Heda said: "So be it."

sentences.zh: 遂入見。

translations.literal: They then entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: They then entered audience.

sentences.zh: 上問卿等所議若何，合達敷奏，其言甚多，大概言河中之事與前日上奏時勢不同，所奏亦不敢自主，議遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor asked what they had deliberated; Heda presented at length, roughly saying affairs in the Middle He differed from when he had memorialized before, and he dared not decide alone—the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked their conclusion; Heda spoke at length, saying the Middle He situation differed from his earlier memorial and he dared not decide—the plan died.

sentences.zh: 二相還陝，量以軍馬出冷水谷，奉行故事而已。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers returned to Shaan and sent what troops they could to Cold Water Valley, observing form only.
translations.idiomatic: Both ministers returned to Shaan and sent troops to Cold Water Valley in mere form.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河中府破。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Middle He prefecture fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Middle He prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 九年，京城被攻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the capital was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the capital was attacked.

sentences.zh: 四月兵退，改元天興。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army withdrew and the era name was changed to Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army withdrew and the era was renamed Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 是月十六日，並樞密院歸尚書省，以宰相兼院官，左右司首領官兼經歷官，惟平章白撒、副樞合喜、院判白華、權院判完顏忽魯剌退罷。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of that month the Bureau of Military Affairs was merged into the Ministry of Revenue, with chief ministers also serving as bureau officers, left and right bureau chiefs as staff officers; only Grand Councilor Bai Sa, Deputy Bureau Judge Hexi, Bureau Judge Bai Hua, and Acting Judge Wanyan Hulula were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth the secret bureau was merged into Revenue, ministers doubling as bureau officers; Grand Councilor Bai Sa, Deputy Hexi, Judge Bai Hua, and Acting Judge Wanyan Hulula alone were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 忽魯剌有口辯，上愛幸之。

translations.literal: Hulula was eloquent and the emperor favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Hulula was glib and the emperor favored him.

sentences.zh: 朝議罪忽魯剌，而書生輩妒華得君，先嘗以語撼之，用是而罷。

translations.literal: Court debate blamed Hulula, but the literati envied Hua's favor and had shaken him with words before, and therefore he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Court blamed Hulula, but scholar-officials jealous of Hua's favor had undermined him, and so he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 金制，樞密院雖主兵，而節制在尚書省。

translations.literal: Under Jin law the secret bureau though commanding troops was controlled by the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: By Jin law the secret bureau commanded troops but Revenue controlled them.

sentences.zh: 兵興以來，茲制漸改，凡是軍事，省官不得預，院官獨任專見，往往敗事。

translations.literal: Since war began this rule gradually changed; all military affairs the provincial officers could not join, bureau officers alone held exclusive views, and affairs were often lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since war began provincial officers were shut out of military affairs and bureau officers alone decided, often to ruin.

sentences.zh: 言者多以為將相權不當分，至是始並之。

translations.literal: Critics long said ministerial and general power should not be divided; only now were they merged.
translations.idiomatic: Critics had long said civil and military power must not be split; now they were united.

sentences.zh: 十二月朔，上遣近侍局提點曳剌粘古即白華所居，問事勢至於此，計將安出。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month the emperor sent Inner Service Bureau director Yelazhangu to Hua's residence to ask, since affairs had come to this, what plan should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the twelfth month the emperor sent Inner Service director Yelazhangu to Hua's home to ask what plan remained now that affairs had reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 華附奏：「今耕稼已廢，糧斛將盡，四外援兵皆不可指擬，車駕當出就外兵。

translations.literal: Hua appended a memorial: "Now farming is abandoned and grain nearly gone; reinforcements from the four directions cannot be counted on; the imperial carriage should go out to join the external armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hua memorialized: "Farming is ruined, grain nearly spent, relief from four sides uncertain—the emperor should go out to the armies.

sentences.zh: 可留皇兄荊王使之監國，任其裁處。

translations.literal: The imperial elder brother the Prince of Jing may be left to oversee the state and decide as he sees fit.
translations.idiomatic: Leave the Prince of Jing to oversee the realm as he judges fit.

sentences.zh: 聖主既出，遣使告語北朝，我出非他處收整軍馬，止以軍卒擅誅唐慶，和議從此斷絕，京師今付之荊王，乞我一二州以老耳。

translations.literal: Once the sage ruler has gone out, send envoys to tell the northern court: our departure is not to gather troops elsewhere but because soldiers on their own killed Tang Qing and peace is broken; the capital is now entrusted to the Prince of Jing; we beg one or two prefectures to live out our old age.
translations.idiomatic: Tell the north: we leave not to gather troops but because soldiers killed Tang Qing and peace is ended; the capital goes to the Prince of Jing; grant us one or two prefectures for our old age.

sentences.zh: 如此則太后皇族可存，正如《春秋》紀季入齊為附庸之事，聖主亦得少寬矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the empress dowager and imperial clan may be preserved, just as in the Spring and Autumn Annals Ji Ji entered Qi as a vassal—the sage ruler may also breathe easier.
translations.idiomatic: So the empress dowager and clan may survive, as Ji Ji entered Qi as a vassal in the Spring and Autumn—the emperor may rest easier.

sentences.zh: 於是起華為右司郎中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hua was made right bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was then made right bureau director.

sentences.zh: 初，親巡之計決，諸將皆預其議，將退，首領官張袞、聶天驥奏：「尚有舊人諳練軍務者，乃置而不用，今所用者，皆不見軍中事體，此為未盡。」

translations.literal: Earlier when the plan for the emperor's personal campaign was decided, all generals took part; as they were about to withdraw, chief officers Zhang Gun and Nie Tianji memorialized: "There are still old hands versed in military affairs who are set aside unused; those now employed do not know army affairs—this is incomplete."
translations.idiomatic: When the personal campaign was decided, all generals took part; on withdrawal Zhang Gun and Nie Tianji said old hands versed in war were unused while newcomers knew nothing of the army.

sentences.zh: 上問未用者何人，皆曰院判白華，上頷之，故有是命。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who was unused; all said Bureau Judge Bai Hua; the emperor nodded, and therefore came this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who was unused, all named Bai Hua; the emperor nodded and appointed him.

sentences.zh: 明日，召華諭之曰：「親巡之計已決，但所往群議未定，有言歸德四面皆水，可以自保者，或言可沿西山入鄧。

translations.literal: The next day Hua was summoned and instructed: "The plan for the personal campaign is decided, but where to go is undecided in the group; some say Guide is surrounded by water on four sides and can protect itself, others say one may follow the western hills into Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Hua was told the personal campaign was fixed but the destination disputed—some said Guide's waters could shelter them, others the western hills into Deng.

sentences.zh: 或言設欲入鄧，大將速不泬今在汝州，不如取陳、蔡路轉往鄧下。

translations.literal: Others say if you wish to enter Deng, the great general Subutai is now at Ru Prefecture, and it is better to take the Chen–Cai route and turn toward Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Others said Subutai at Ru Prefecture made the Chen–Cai route into Deng better.

sentences.zh: 卿以為如何？」

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 華曰：「歸德城雖堅，久而食盡，坐以待斃，決不可往。

translations.literal: Hua said: "Though Guide's walls are strong, in time food will be exhausted and sitting waiting to die—decidedly one must not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hua said: "Guide's walls are strong, but food will fail and waiting means death—do not go.

sentences.zh: 欲往鄧下，既汝州有速不泬，斷不能往。

translations.literal: If you wish to go to Deng, with Subutai at Ru you cannot go.
translations.idiomatic: Deng is impossible with Subutai at Ru.

sentences.zh: 以今日事勢，博徒所謂孤注者也。

translations.literal: Given today's situation, it is what gamblers call staking all on one throw.
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation is the gambler's last stake.

sentences.zh: 孤注雲者，止有背城之戰。

translations.literal: Staking all means only fighting with one's back to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Staking all means only battle with backs to the wall.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，當直赴汝州，與之一決，有楚則無漢，有漢則無楚。

translations.literal: For the present plan one should go straight to Ru Prefecture and settle it in one fight—where Chu is, Han is not; where Han is, Chu is not.
translations.idiomatic: Go straight to Ru and decide in one fight—Chu or Han, not both.

sentences.zh: 汝州戰不如半途戰，半途戰又不如出城戰，所以然者何？

translations.literal: Better to fight at Ru than halfway, and better halfway than leaving the city—why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Better at Ru than halfway, better halfway than from the walls—why?

sentences.zh: 我軍食力猶在，馬則豆力猶在。

translations.literal: Our army's strength in food still holds, and the horses still have bean fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Our men still have food strength; horses still have bean fodder.

sentences.zh: 若出京益遠，軍食日減，馬食野草，事益難矣。

translations.literal: The farther from the capital, the less army food day by day; horses eat wild grass and affairs grow harder.
translations.idiomatic: Farther from the capital, army food dwindles daily; horses eat wild grass and all grows harder.

sentences.zh: 若我軍便得戰，存亡決此一舉，外則可以激三軍之氣，內則可以慰都人之心。

translations.literal: If our army can fight at once, survival hangs on this one throw; outward it can stir the three armies' spirit, inward it can comfort the capital's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: One fight decides survival, stirs the armies without, comforts the capital within.

sentences.zh: 或止為避遷之計，人心顧戀家業，未必毅然從行。

translations.literal: If it is only a plan to flee, men will cling to their homes and may not follow resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: If it is only flight, men will cling to home and may not follow boldly.

sentences.zh: 可詳審之。」

translations.literal: This may be weighed carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Weigh this carefully."

sentences.zh: 遂召諸相及首領官同議，禾速嘉兀地不、元帥豬兒、高顯、王義深俱主歸德之議，丞相賽不主鄧，議竟不能決。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers and chief officers were summoned to deliberate together; Hesujia Wudibu, commander Zhuer, Gao Xian, and Wang Yishen all favored Guide, Chief Minister Sai favored Deng, and deliberation could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and chiefs were summoned; Hesujia, Zhuer, Gao Xian, and Wang Yishen favored Guide, Sai favored Deng—no decision.

sentences.zh: 明日，制旨京城食盡，今擬親出，聚集軍士于大慶殿諭以此意，諭訖，諸帥將佐合辭奏曰：「聖主不可親出，止可命將，三軍欣然願為國家效死。」

translations.literal: The next day an edict said the capital's food was gone and the emperor would go out in person; troops were gathered at Daqing Hall and told; when the address ended, commanders and staff together memorialized: "The sage ruler must not go out in person; only command generals—the three armies gladly die for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Next day an edict said food was gone and the emperor would go out; at Daqing Hall the troops were told; commanders memorialized: "The emperor must not go out—send generals; the armies will die gladly."

sentences.zh: 上猶豫，欲以官奴為馬軍帥，高顯為步軍帥，劉益副之，蓋采輿議也，而三人者亦欲奉命。

translations.literal: The emperor still hesitated, wishing to make Guannu cavalry commander and Gao Xian infantry commander with Liu Yi as deputy—adopting the carriage ministers' view—and the three were willing to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated, wishing Guannu for horse and Gao Xian for foot with Liu Yi deputy—the carriage view—and all three would accept.

sentences.zh: 權參政內族訛出大罵云：「汝輩把鋤不知高下，國家大事，敢易承邪！」

translations.literal: Acting Councilor the clansman Echu cursed loudly: "You lot wield hoes and know not high from low—dare you lightly undertake the state's great affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Acting councilor clansman Echu cursed: "You wield hoes and know nothing of state affairs—dare you take this on!"

sentences.zh: 眾默然，惟官奴曰：「若將相可了，何至使我輩。」

translations.literal: All were silent; only Guannu said: "If ministers and generals could finish it, why reach us."
translations.idiomatic: All were silent; only Guannu said: "If ministers and generals could manage, why us."

sentences.zh: 事亦中止。

translations.literal: The matter also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That too ceased.

sentences.zh: 明日，民間哄傳車駕欲奉皇太后及妃後往歸德，軍士家屬留後。

translations.literal: The next day the populace buzzed that the imperial carriage would escort the empress dowager and consorts to Guide while soldiers' families were left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Next day rumor said the carriage would escort the empress dowager and consorts to Guide while families stayed.

sentences.zh: 目今食盡，坐視城中俱餓死矣。

translations.literal: Now food is gone—we sit watching the whole city starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: Food is gone—we watch the whole city starve.

sentences.zh: 縱能至歸德，軍馬所費支吾復得幾許日。

translations.literal: Even if we reach Guide, how many days can army expenses be stretched?
translations.idiomatic: Even at Guide, how long will army costs last?

sentences.zh: 上聞之，召賽不、合周、訛出、烏古孫卜吉、完顏正夫議，餘人不預。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and summoned Sai, Hezhou, Echu, Wugusun Buji, and Wanyan Zhengfu to deliberate; the rest were not included.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Sai, Hezhou, Echu, Wugusun Buji, and Wanyan Zhengfu alone.

sentences.zh: 移時方出，見首領官、丞相言，前日巡守之議已定，止為一白華都改卻，今往汝州就軍馬索戰去矣。

translations.literal: After a long while they emerged and told the chief officers and chief minister: the other day's patrol plan was fixed, but Bai Hua alone changed it; now they go to Ru to seek battle with the armies.
translations.idiomatic: They emerged and told chiefs and minister: the patrol plan was fixed until Bai Hua alone changed it; now they go to Ru for battle.

sentences.zh: 遂擇日祭太廟誓師，擬以二十五之日啟行。

translations.literal: A day was chosen to sacrifice at the ancestral temple and swear the army; they planned to set out on the twenty-fifth.
translations.idiomatic: They chose a day for ancestral sacrifice and army oath, planning to depart on the twenty-fifth.

sentences.zh: 是月晦，車駕至黃陵岡，復有北幸之議，語在《白撒傳》。

translations.literal: At month's end the imperial carriage reached Huangling Mound; there was again talk of going north—the account is in the biography of Bai Sa.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end the carriage reached Huangling Mound; northward talk arose again—see the biography of Bai Sa.

sentences.zh: 天興二年正月朔，上次黃陵岡，就歸德餫船北渡，諸相共奏，京師及河南諸州聞上幸河北，恐生他變，可下詔安撫之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of Tianxing year two the emperor halted at Huangling Mound and crossed north on Guide supply boats; the chief ministers together memorialized that Jingzhao and the Henan prefectures, hearing the emperor favored Hebei, might change otherwise, and an edict should reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: On Tianxing year two, first month, first day, the emperor halted at Huangling Mound and crossed north on Guide grain boats; ministers said Henan might change on hearing Hebei favor and begged reassuring edicts.

sentences.zh: 是時，在所父老僧道獻食，及牛酒犒軍者相屬，上親為拊慰，人人為之感泣。

translations.literal: At that time elders, monks, and Daoists where they were offered food and oxen and wine to reward the army in succession; the emperor personally comforted them, and every man wept.
translations.idiomatic: Elders, monks, and Daoists offered food, oxen, and wine in turn; the emperor comforted them and all wept.

sentences.zh: 乃赦河朔，招集兵糧，赦文條畫十餘款，分道傳送。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pardoned Hebei, summoned troops and grain, and the amnesty had more than ten articles sent by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned Hebei, summoned troops and grain, and sent an amnesty of more than ten articles by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 二日，或有云：「昨所發河南詔書，倘落大軍中，奈泄事機何。」

translations.literal: On the second day someone said: "Yesterday's Henan edict—if it falls into the great army's hands, how can we keep plans secret?"
translations.idiomatic: On the second day someone said: "Yesterday's Henan edict—if the great army seizes it, our plans are exposed."

sentences.zh: 上怒，委近侍局官傳旨，謂首領官張袞、白華、內族訛可當發詔時不為後慮，皆量決之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and entrusted Inner Service officers to transmit the edict that chief officer Zhang Gun, Bai Hua, and clansman Eke, when issuing the edict, had not considered afterward—all were sentenced by measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and had Inner Service officers sentence Zhang Gun, Bai Hua, and clansman Eke for not foreseeing this when issuing the edict.

sentences.zh: 是時衛州軍兩日至蒲城，而大軍徐躡其後。

translations.literal: At that time Weizhou troops reached Pucheng in two days while the great army slowly followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou troops reached Pucheng in two days while the great army followed slowly.

sentences.zh: 十五日，宰相諸帥共議上前，郎中完顏胡魯剌秉筆書，某軍前鋒，某軍殿后，餘事皆有條畫。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth the chief ministers and commanders together deliberated before the emperor; director Wanyan Hulula took brush and wrote which army vanguard, which rear guard, and the rest in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth ministers and commanders deliberated before the emperor; director Wanyan Hulula wrote vanguard, rear, and the rest in order.

sentences.zh: 書畢，惟不言所往，華私問胡魯剌，托以不知。

translations.literal: When writing was finished they alone did not say where they were going; Hua privately asked Hulula, who pleaded ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: When done they did not say the destination; Hua asked Hulula privately, who pleaded ignorance.

sentences.zh: 是晚，平章及諸帥還蒲城軍中。

translations.literal: That evening the grand councilor and commanders returned to the Pucheng army.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the grand councilor and commanders returned to Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 夜半，訛可、袞就華帳中呼華云：「上已登舟，君不知之耶？」

translations.literal: At midnight Eke and Gun came to Hua's tent calling: "The emperor has already boarded the boat—do you not know?"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Eke and Gun called at Hua's tent: "The emperor has boarded—do you not know?"

sentences.zh: 華遂問其由，訛可云：「我昨日已知上欲與李左丞、完顏郎中先下歸德，令諸軍並北岸行，至鳳池渡河。

translations.literal: Hua then asked the reason; Eke said: "Yesterday I knew the emperor wished to go down to Guide first with Left Councilor Li and Director Wanyan, ordering all armies to march on the north bank and cross at Fengchi.
translations.idiomatic: Hua asked why; Eke said: "Yesterday I knew the emperor meant to reach Guide first with Councilor Li and Director Wanyan, armies on the north bank crossing at Fengchi.

sentences.zh: 今夜平章及禾速嘉、元帥官奴等來，言大軍在蒲城曾與金軍接戰，勢莫能支，遂擁主上登舟，軍資一切委棄，止令忠孝軍上船，馬悉留營中。

translations.literal: Tonight the grand councilor and Hesujia, commander Guannu, and others came saying the great army at Pucheng had engaged Jin troops and could not hold, and they crowded the emperor onto the boat, abandoning all army stores, ordering only the Loyal and Filial Army aboard while horses were all left in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Tonight the grand councilor, Hesujia, Guannu, and others said the great army at Pucheng had fought Jin troops and could not hold, crowded the emperor onto the boat, abandoned stores, put only the Loyal and Filial Army aboard, and left all horses in camp.

sentences.zh: 計舟已行數里矣。」

translations.literal: They reckoned the boat had already gone several li.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned the boat had already gone several li.

sentences.zh: 華又問：「公何不從往？」

translations.literal: Hua again asked: "Why did you not follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua asked: "Why did you not follow?"

sentences.zh: 云：「昨日擬定首領官止令胡魯剌登舟，余悉隨軍，用是不敢。」

translations.literal: He said: "Yesterday it was fixed that only Hulula of the chief officers should board; the rest were to follow the army, and therefore I dared not."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Yesterday only Hulula of the chiefs was to board; the rest followed the army, and I dared not."

sentences.zh: 是夜，總帥百家領諸軍舟往鳳池，大軍覺之，兵遂潰。

translations.literal: That night commander-in-chief Bai led all army boats toward Fengchi; the great army noticed and the troops thereupon collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: That night commander Bai led all army boats to Fengchi; the great army noticed and the troops collapsed.

sentences.zh: 上在歸德。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Guide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Guide.

sentences.zh: 三月，崔立以汴京降，右宣徽提點近侍局移剌粘古謀之鄧，上不聽。

translations.literal: In the third month Cui Li surrendered Bianjing; Right Palace Director and Inner Service director Yelazhangu plotted going to Deng, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Cui Li surrendered Bianjing; Inner Service director Yelazhangu plotted Deng, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時粘古之兄瑗為鄧州節度使、兼行樞密院事，其子與粘古之子並從駕為衛士。

translations.literal: At that time Zhangu's elder brother Yuan was Deng prefectural military commissioner and also acting secret bureau judge; his son and Zhangu's son both followed the carriage as guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangu's brother Yuan was Deng commissioner and acting secret bureau judge; both sons followed as guards.

sentences.zh: 適朝廷將召鄧兵入援，粘古因與華謀同之鄧，且拉其二子以往，上覺之，獨命華行，而粘古改之徐州。

translations.literal: Just then the court was about to summon Deng troops for relief; Zhangu therefore plotted with Hua to go to Deng together and drag both sons along; the emperor noticed and ordered Hua alone to go while Zhangu was reassigned to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court was summoning Deng relief; Zhangu plotted with Hua to go to Deng and take both sons; the emperor noticed, sent Hua alone, and reassigned Zhangu to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 華既至鄧，以事久不濟，淹留於館，遂若無意於世者。

translations.literal: When Hua reached Deng, as affairs dragged on without success he lingered at the guesthouse and seemed to have no care for the world.
translations.idiomatic: At Deng, affairs long unresolved, Hua lingered at the guesthouse as if the world did not concern him.

sentences.zh: 會瑗以鄧入宋，華亦從至襄陽，宋署為制幹，又改均州提督。

translations.literal: When Yuan brought Deng to the Song, Hua also followed to Xiangyang; the Song appointed him staff officer, then changed him to supervisor of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan brought Deng to the Song, Hua followed to Xiangyang; the Song made him staff officer, then Jun prefectural supervisor.

sentences.zh: 後范用吉殺均之長吏。

translations.literal: Later Fan Yongji killed Jun's senior official.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan Yongji killed Jun's senior official.

sentences.zh: 送款於北朝，遂因而北歸。

translations.literal: He offered surrender to the northern court and thereupon returned north.
translations.idiomatic: He offered surrender to the northern court and returned north.

sentences.zh: 士大夫以華夙儒貴顯，國危不能以義自處為貶云。

translations.literal: The scholar-officials, because Hua had long been a Confucian of noble rank, criticized that when the state was in peril he could not comport himself by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials, noting Hua's long standing as a prominent Confucian, faulted him for not holding to righteousness when the state was in peril.

sentences.zh: 用吉者，本姓孛術魯，名久住。

translations.literal: Yongji's original surname was Boluolu, name Jiuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji was originally surnamed Boluolu and named Jiuzhu.

sentences.zh: 初歸入宋，謁制置趙範，將以計動其心，故更姓名范用吉。

translations.literal: When he first entered Song service he called on Commissioner Zhao Fan, intending to sway his mind with a stratagem, and therefore changed his name to Fan Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering Song service he visited Commissioner Zhao Fan, planning to sway him, and changed his name to Fan Yongji.

sentences.zh: 趙怒其觸諱，斥之，用吉猶應對如故。

translations.literal: Zhao was angry that he had touched the taboo of his name and drove him off; Yongji answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, angered that he had touched the taboo of Fan's name, drove him off; Yongji answered as before.

sentences.zh: 趙良久方悟，且利其事與己符，遂擢置左右，凡所言動，略不加疑，遂易其姓曰花，使為太尉，改鎮均州。

translations.literal: After a long while Zhao finally understood and, seeing profit in affairs matching his own wishes, promoted him to his side; whatever he said or did was scarcely doubted; he then changed his surname to Hua, made him Grand Marshal, and transferred him to garrison Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After long reflection Zhao understood, saw profit in what matched his wishes, and kept Yongji at his side without doubt; he changed his surname to Hua, made him Grand Marshal, and transferred him to Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，納款於北。

translations.literal: Before long he offered surrender to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he offered surrender to the north.

sentences.zh: 後以家人誣以欲叛，為同列所害。

translations.literal: Later his household falsely accused him of wishing to rebel, and he was killed by his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Later his household falsely accused him of rebellion, and colleagues killed him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：白華以儒者習吏事，以經生知兵，其所論建，屢中事機，然三軍敗衄之餘，士氣不作，其言果可行乎。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Bai Hua, as a Confucian practiced in clerical affairs and as a classicist who knew warfare, in what he proposed and built repeatedly hit the moment—yet after the three armies' defeats morale did not rise; could his words truly have been carried out?
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Bai Hua, a Confucian versed in administration and a classicist who understood war, repeatedly hit the mark in counsel—yet after repeated defeats morale never rallied; could his plans truly have been executed?

sentences.zh: 從瑗歸宋，聲名掃地，則猶得列于金臣之傳者，援蜀譙周等例云。

translations.literal: Following Yuan to the Song, his reputation was swept away—yet he may still be listed among Jin ministers' biographies by the precedent of Shu's Qiao Zhou and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yuan to the Song ruined his reputation—yet he may still appear among Jin ministers' biographies by the precedent of Qiao Zhou of Shu and the like.

sentences.zh: 斜卯愛實

translations.literal: Xiemao Aishi
translations.idiomatic: Xiemao Aishi

sentences.zh: 斜卯愛實，字正之，策論進士也。

translations.literal: Xiemao Aishi, style name Zhengzhi, was a policy-essay advanced scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Xiemao Aishi, styled Zhengzhi, was a policy-essay advanced scholar.

sentences.zh: 正大間，累官翰林直學士，兼左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda period he rose through offices to Hanlin Academician Expositor and concurrently left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengda period he rose to Hanlin Academician Expositor and concurrently left bureau director.

sentences.zh: 天興元年正月，聞大兵將至，以點檢夾穀撒合為總帥，率步騎三萬巡河渡，命宿直將軍內族長樂權近侍局使，監其軍。

translations.literal: In the first month of Tianxing year one, hearing the great army was about to arrive, he made Inspector Jiagu Sahe commander-in-chief, leading thirty thousand foot and horse to patrol the river crossings, and ordered the duty general, clansman Changle, acting Inner Service director, to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year one, first month, hearing the great army was coming, he made Inspector Jiagu Sahe commander with thirty thousand foot and horse to patrol the river crossings, with duty general clansman Changle, acting Inner Service director, to supervise.

sentences.zh: 行至封丘而還。

translations.literal: They reached Fengqiu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Fengqiu and returned.

sentences.zh: 入自梁門，樞密副使合喜遇之，笑語撒合曰：「吾言信矣，當為我作主人。」

translations.literal: Entering by the Liang Gate, Deputy Bureau Judge Hexi met them and said laughing to Sahe: "My words were true—you must play host for me."
translations.idiomatic: Entering by the Liang Gate, Deputy Judge Hexi met them and laughed to Sahe: "I told you so—you must host me.

sentences.zh: 蓋世俗酬謝之意也。

translations.literal: This was the meaning of worldly thanks and repayment.
translations.idiomatic: This was worldly thanks and repayment.

sentences.zh: 明日，大兵遂合，朝廷置而不問。

translations.literal: The next day the great army closed in, and the court set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the great army closed in, and the court ignored it.

sentences.zh: 於是愛實上言曰：「撒合統兵三萬，本欲乘大兵遠至，喘息未定而擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Aishi memorialized: "Sahe commanded thirty thousand men, intending to strike while the great army had come far and had not yet caught breath.
translations.idiomatic: Aishi memorialized: "Sahe led thirty thousand meant to strike while the great army, far from home, had not caught breath.

sentences.zh: 出京才數十里，不逢一人騎，已畏縮不敢進。

translations.literal: Leaving the capital only a few tens of li, not meeting a single rider, he already shrank back and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: A few tens of li from the capital, without meeting a single rider, he already shrank back and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 設遇大兵，其肯用命乎？

translations.literal: If he met the great army, would he be willing to give his life?
translations.idiomatic: If he met the great army, would he fight to the death?

sentences.zh: 乞斬二人以肅軍政。」

translations.literal: I beg execute the two men to stiffen military discipline."
translations.idiomatic: I beg execute both to stiffen discipline."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply.

sentences.zh: 蓋合喜輩以京師倚此一軍為命，初不敢俾之出戰，特以外議哄然，故暫出以應之云。

translations.literal: For Hexi and his ilk the capital relied on this one army as its life; at first they dared not let it fight; only because outside talk buzzed did they go out briefly to answer it.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi and his circle relied on this army for the capital's life and dared not let it fight; they went out briefly only to answer public clamor.

sentences.zh: 衛紹、鎬厲二王家屬，皆以兵防護，且設官提控，巡警之嚴過於獄犴。

translations.literal: The households of the princes of Wei and Hao were all guarded by troops, with officials appointed to oversee them; patrol was stricter than a prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei and Hao princely households were guarded by troops with overseers; patrol was stricter than a prison.

sentences.zh: 至是，衛紹宅二十年，鎬厲宅四十年。

translations.literal: By then the Wei household had been confined twenty years, the Hao forty.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Wei house had been confined twenty years, the Hao forty.

sentences.zh: 正大間，朝臣屢有言及者，不報。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda period court ministers repeatedly spoke of it without reply.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda ministers repeatedly spoke of it without reply.

sentences.zh: 愛實乃上言曰：「二族衰微，無異匹庶，假欲為不善，孰與同惡？

translations.literal: Aishi then memorialized: "The two clans have declined and are no different from commoners; even if they wished ill, who would join them in evil?
translations.idiomatic: Aishi memorialized: "The two clans have declined like commoners; who would join them in evil?

sentences.zh: 男女婚嫁，人之大欲，豈有幽囚終世，永無伉儷之望，在他人尚且不忍，況骨肉乎！」

translations.literal: Men and women marrying is humanity's great desire—can they be shut in forever without hope of spouses? Others could not bear it—how much less kin!"
translations.idiomatic: Marriage is humanity's great desire—can they be shut in forever without spouses? Others would not bear it—how much less kin!

sentences.zh: 哀宗感其言，始聽自便。

translations.literal: The Emperor Aizong was moved by his words and at last allowed them freedom.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong was moved and at last allowed them freedom.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有青城之難。

translations.literal: Before long came the calamity at Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the calamity at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 愛實憤時相非其人，嘗歷數曰：「平章白撒固權市恩，擊丸外百無一能。
