translations.literal: Aishi resented that the chief ministers were not the right men and once enumerated them: "Grand Councilor Bai Sa indeed trades in favors by power; apart from playing ball he is capable of nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Aishi resented unfit chief ministers and once listed them: "Grand Councilor Bai Sa trades in favors by power; apart from ball games he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 丞相賽不菽麥不分，更謂乏材，亦不至此人為相。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Sai cannot tell beans from wheat; even calling talent scarce, he should not have reached the post of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Sai cannot tell beans from wheat; even with scarce talent he should not be chief minister.

sentences.zh: 參政兼樞密副使赤盞合喜粗暴，一馬軍之材止矣，乃令兼將相之權。

translations.literal: Acting councilor and Deputy Bureau Judge Chisan Hexi is brutal—talent for a single horse army at most—yet he is given combined civil and military power.
translations.idiomatic: Acting councilor and Deputy Judge Chisan Hexi is brutal—fit for one horse army at most—yet holds civil and military power together.

sentences.zh: 右丞顏盞世魯居相位已七八年，碌碌無補，備員而已。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yansai Shilu has sat in office seven or eight years, achieving nothing, a placeholder only.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yansai Shilu has sat in office seven or eight years, achieving nothing—a placeholder.

sentences.zh: 患難之際，倚注此類，欲冀中興，難矣。」

translations.literal: In time of peril to rely on such men and hope for restoration is hard.
translations.idiomatic: In peril to rely on such men and hope for restoration is hard.

sentences.zh: 於是世魯罷相，賽不乞致仕，而白撒、合喜不恤也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shilu was dismissed from the chief ministry, Sai begged retirement, while Bai Sa and Hexi paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu left the chief ministry, Sai begged retirement, while Bai Sa and Hexi paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，京城罷攻，大兵退。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year the capital siege was lifted and the great army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year the siege of the capital was lifted and the great army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既而以害唐慶事，和議遂絕。

translations.literal: Then because of the killing of Tang Qing, peace talks were broken off.
translations.idiomatic: Then, because of the killing of Tang Qing, peace was broken off.

sentences.zh: 於是再簽民兵為守禦備。

translations.literal: Thereupon militia were again mustered for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Militia were again mustered for defense.

sentences.zh: 八月，括京城粟，以轉運使完顏珠顆、張俊民、曳剌克忠等置局，以推舉為名，珠顆諭民曰：「汝等當從實推唱，果如一旦糧盡，令汝妻子作軍食，復能吝否？」

translations.literal: In the eighth month grain in the capital was seized; Transport Commissioner Wanyan Zhuguo, Zhang Junmin, Yelazhangu, and others set up offices under the name of recommendation; Zhuguo told the people: "You must report truthfully; if grain is truly exhausted one day and you are told to make your wives and children army food, can you still be stingy?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month grain in the capital was seized; Transport Commissioner Wanyan Zhuguo, Zhang Junmin, Yelazhangu, and others set up offices in the name of recommendation; Zhuguo told the people: "Report truthfully; if grain is exhausted and you are told to make wives and children army food, can you still be stingy?

sentences.zh: 既而罷括粟令，復以進獻取之。

translations.literal: Before long the grain-seizure order was stopped and grain was taken again as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the seizure order stopped and grain was taken again as tribute.

sentences.zh: 前御史大夫內族合周復冀進用，建言京城括粟可得百餘萬石。

translations.literal: Former Censor-in-Chief clansman Hezhou again hoped for advancement and proposed that seizing capital grain could yield more than a million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Former Censor-in-Chief clansman Hezhou again hoped for advancement and said seizing capital grain could yield more than a million shi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷信之，命權參知政事，與左丞李蹊總其事。

translations.literal: The court believed him and appointed him acting Councilor, with Left Vice Director Li Xi to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed him and made him acting councilor, with Left Vice Director Li Xi to oversee.

sentences.zh: 先令各家自實，壯者存石有三斗，幼者半之，仍書其數門首，敢有匿者以升斗論罪。

translations.literal: First each household was to report its own stores; adults were to keep three dou of beans, children half, and the amount was written on the door; concealment was punished by the peck and quart.
translations.idiomatic: Each household first reported its stores; adults kept three dou of beans, children half, the amount written on the door; concealment was punished by measure.

sentences.zh: 京城三十六坊，各選深刻者主之，內族完顏久住尤酷暴。

translations.literal: Thirty-six wards of the capital each chose harsh men to oversee them; clansman Wanyan Jiuzhu was especially cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six wards each chose harsh overseers; clansman Wanyan Jiuzhu was especially cruel.

sentences.zh: 有寡婦二口，實豆六斗，內有蓬子約三升，久住笑曰：「吾得之矣。」

translations.literal: A widow of two mouths had in fact six dou of beans, with about three sheng of grass seed mixed in; Jiuzhu laughed and said: "I have got it."
translations.idiomatic: A widow of two mouths had six dou of beans with about three sheng of grass seed mixed in; Jiuzhu laughed: "I have it.

sentences.zh: 執而以令於眾。

translations.literal: He seized her and announced the order to the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He seized her and announced it to the crowd.

sentences.zh: 婦泣訴曰：「妾夫死于兵，姑老不能為養，故雜蓬粃以自食耳，非敢以為軍儲也。

translations.literal: The woman wept and pleaded: "My husband died in the army; my mother-in-law is old and cannot be fed; I mixed grass chaff to eat myself—not daring to make army stores.
translations.idiomatic: She wept: "My husband died in the army; my mother-in-law cannot be fed; I mixed chaff to eat—not for army stores.

sentences.zh: 且三升，六斗之餘。」

translations.literal: And it is three sheng, the remainder of six dou."
translations.idiomatic: And it is three sheng, the remainder of six dou.

sentences.zh: 不從，竟死杖下。

translations.literal: He would not listen and she died under the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen and she died under the staff.

sentences.zh: 京師聞之股栗，盡投其餘於糞溷中。

translations.literal: The capital trembled at the news and threw the rest into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: The capital trembled and threw the rest into privies.

sentences.zh: 或白于李蹊，蹊顰蹙曰：「白之參政。」

translations.literal: Someone told Li Xi; Xi frowned and said: "Tell the acting councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Li Xi; Xi frowned: "Tell the acting councilor.

sentences.zh: 其人即白合周，周曰：「人云『花又不損，蜜又得成』。

translations.literal: The man told Hezhou at once; Hezhou said: "People say, 'The flower is unharmed and the honey is still made.
translations.idiomatic: He told Hezhou; Hezhou said: "People say, 'The flower is unharmed and honey is still made.

sentences.zh: 予謂花不損，何由成蜜？

translations.literal: I say if the flower is unharmed, how can honey be made?
translations.idiomatic: I say if the flower is unharmed, how is honey made?

sentences.zh: 且京師危急，今欲存社稷耶？

translations.literal: And the capital is in peril—do you wish to preserve the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: The capital is in peril—do you wish to preserve the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 存百姓耶？」

translations.literal: Or preserve the people?"
translations.idiomatic: Or preserve the people?"

sentences.zh: 當時皆莫敢言，愛實遂上奏，大概言：「罷括粟，則改虐政為仁政，散怨氣為和氣。」

translations.literal: At the time none dared speak; Aishi then memorialized, roughly saying: "Stop seizing grain, then change cruel government into humane government and scattered resentment into harmony."
translations.idiomatic: None dared speak; Aishi memorialized: stop seizing grain, change cruel rule into humane rule and scattered resentment into harmony.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply.

sentences.zh: 時所括不能三萬斛，而京城益蕭然矣。

translations.literal: What was seized could not reach thirty thousand hu, and the capital grew more desolate.
translations.idiomatic: What was seized did not reach thirty thousand hu, and the capital grew more desolate.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，死者相枕，貧富束手待斃而已。

translations.literal: From then on the dead lay pillow to pillow; rich and poor alike waited hands bound to starve.
translations.idiomatic: From then the dead lay pillow to pillow; rich and poor waited to starve.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，命出太倉米作粥以食餓者，愛實聞之歎曰：「與其食之，寧如勿奪。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and ordered grain from the great storehouse made into porridge to feed the hungry; Aishi heard and sighed: "Better not to seize than to feed afterward."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered great-storehouse grain made into porridge for the hungry; Aishi sighed: "Better not to seize than to feed afterward.

sentences.zh: 為奉御把奴所告。

translations.literal: He was reported by attendant Ba Nu.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Ba Nu reported him.

sentences.zh: 又近侍干預朝政，愛實上章諫曰：「今近侍權太重，將相大臣不敢與之相抗 。

translations.literal: Again inner attendants interfered in court government; Aishi memorialized in remonstrance: "Today inner attendants' power is too heavy; chief ministers and generals dare not resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants again interfered in government; Aishi remonstrated: "Inner attendants' power is too heavy; ministers and generals dare not resist.

sentences.zh: 自古僕禦之臣不過供給指使而已，雖名僕臣，亦必選擇正人。

translations.literal: Since antiquity servant and groom officials have been no more than for supply and orders; though called servant ministers, upright men must be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity grooms and servants supplied and obeyed only; though called ministers, upright men must be chosen.

sentences.zh: 今不論賢否，惟以世胄或吏員為之。

translations.literal: Now without regard for worth they are made only from noble houses or clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Now without regard for worth they are taken only from noble houses or clerks.

sentences.zh: 夫給使令之材，使預社稷大計，此輩果何所知乎。」

translations.literal: Talent for running errands—yet to entrust them with great plans for the altars—what do such men know?"
translations.idiomatic: Talent for errands—yet the altars' great plans are entrusted to them—what do they know?

sentences.zh: 章既上，近侍數人泣訴上前曰：「愛實以臣等為奴隸，置至尊何地耶！」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, several inner attendants wept before the emperor: "Aishi treats us as slaves—where does he place Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was in, several inner attendants wept before the emperor: "Aishi treats us as slaves—where does he place Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 上益怒，送有司。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier and handed him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier and handed him to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 近侍局副使李大節從容開釋，乃赦之，出為中京留守，後不知所終。

translations.literal: Inner Service deputy Li Dajie calmly secured his release; he was pardoned and sent out as Zhongjing defender; later his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Service deputy Li Dajie secured his release; he was pardoned and made Zhongjing defender; later his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 附:合周

translations.literal: Appendix: Hezhou
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Hezhou

sentences.zh: 合周者，一名永錫。

translations.literal: Hezhou, also named Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou, also named Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 貞祐中，為元帥左監軍，失援中都，宣宗削除官爵，杖之八十。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou he was left deputy army commander; failing to relieve Zhongdu, Emperor Xuanzong stripped rank and office and beat him eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou he was left deputy army commander; failing to relieve Zhongdu, Emperor Xuanzong stripped rank and beat him eighty strokes.

sentences.zh: 已而復用。

translations.literal: Before long he was used again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was used again.

sentences.zh: 四年，以御史大夫權尚書右丞，總兵陝西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, as Censor-in-Chief he acted as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and commanded troops in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as censor-in-chief he acted as right vice director of Revenue and commanded troops in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 合周留澠池數日，進及京兆，而大兵已至，合周竟不出兵，遂失潼關。

translations.literal: Hezhou lingered at Mianchi several days, advanced to Jingzhao, but the great army had already arrived; Hezhou in the end did not send troops and lost Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou lingered at Mianchi, advanced to Jingzhao, but the great army had arrived; he sent no troops and lost Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 有司以敵至不出兵當斬，諸皇族百餘人上章救之，上曰：「向合周救中都，未至而軍潰，使宗廟山陵失守，罪當誅，朕特寬貸以全其命。

translations.literal: The authorities said that when the enemy arrived he should have sent troops and deserved execution; more than a hundred of the imperial clan memorialized to save him; the emperor said: "Formerly Hezhou went to relieve Zhongdu, did not arrive, and the army collapsed, letting the ancestral temples and imperial tombs be lost—the crime deserved death; I specially pardoned to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities said failure to march when the enemy came deserved death; more than a hundred of the clan memorialized; the emperor said: "When Hezhou went to relieve Zhongdu he did not arrive and the army collapsed, losing temples and tombs—a crime deserving death; I pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋復重職，今鎮陝西，所犯乃爾，國家大法，豈敢私耶！」

translations.literal: Soon he was again given heavy office; now garrisoning Shaanxi he offends thus—state law, how can I favor him privately!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again given heavy office; now garrisoning Shaanxi he offends thus—how can state law favor him!"

sentences.zh: 遂再奪爵，免死除名。

translations.literal: His rank was again stripped, death remitted, name removed.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was again stripped, death remitted, name removed.

sentences.zh: 至是，為參知政事。

translations.literal: By then he was acting councilor.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was acting councilor.

sentences.zh: 性好作詩詞，語鄙俚，人采其語以為戲笑。

translations.literal: By nature he loved composing lyrics; the language was vulgar, and people took his lines for jest.
translations.idiomatic: He loved composing lyrics in vulgar language, and people quoted him in jest.

sentences.zh: 因自草《括粟榜文》，有「雀無翅兒不飛，蛇無頭兒不行」等語，以「而」作「兒」，掾史知之，不敢易也。

translations.literal: He himself drafted the proclamation for seizing grain with lines such as "sparrows have no wings and cannot fly, snakes have no heads and cannot go," using "er" for "er"—the clerks knew but dared not change it.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the grain-seizure proclamation with lines such as "sparrows have no wings and cannot fly, snakes have no heads and cannot go," using colloquial "er"—clerks knew but dared not change it.

sentences.zh: 京城目之曰「雀兒參政」。

translations.literal: The capital called him "Sparrow Acting Councilor."
translations.idiomatic: The capital called him "Sparrow Acting Councilor."

sentences.zh: 哀宗用而不悟，竟致敗事。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong used him without understanding and in the end affairs were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong used him without understanding and affairs were ruined.

sentences.zh: 石抹世勣

translations.literal: Shimoshi Ji
translations.idiomatic: Shimoshi Ji

sentences.zh: 石抹世勣，字景略。

translations.literal: Shimoshi Ji, style name Jinglue.
translations.idiomatic: Shimoshi Ji, styled Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 幼勤學，為文有體裁。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently; his writing had form.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied hard; his writing had form.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，以父元毅死王事，收充擎執。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengan, because his father Yuanyi died in the king's service, he was enrolled as an attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan year two, because his father Yuanyi died in the king's service, he was enrolled as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 五年，登詞賦、經義兩科進士第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he passed both the rhapsody and classics advanced examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he passed both the rhapsody and classics examinations.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，累官為太常丞，預講議所事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and took part in deliberations of the Discussion Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year three he rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and joined the Discussion Office.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷徙河北軍戶河南，宰職議給以田，世勣上言曰：「荒閑之田及牧馬地，其始耕墾，費力當倍，一歲斷不能熟。

translations.literal: At that time the court moved Hebei army households to Henan; the chief ministers deliberated giving them fields; Ji memorialized: "Wasteland and horse pasture, at first plowing and opening, cost double the labor—a year cannot bring it to ripeness.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved Hebei army households to Henan, ministers deliberated giving them fields; Ji said: "Wasteland and horse pasture cost double to open—a year cannot ripen it.

sentences.zh: 若奪民素蒔者與之，則民將失所，且啟不和之端。

translations.literal: If you take what commoners have long planted and give it to them, the people will lose their place and the seeds of discord will open.
translations.idiomatic: If you take what commoners have long planted, the people lose their place and discord opens.

sentences.zh: 況軍戶率無耕牛，雖或有之，而廩給未敢遽減。

translations.literal: Moreover army households mostly lack plow oxen; even if they have them, grain allowance cannot be quickly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Army households mostly lack oxen; even if they have them, grain allowance cannot be quickly cut.

sentences.zh: 彼既南來，所捐田宅為人所有，一旦北歸，能無爭奪？

translations.literal: Having come south, the fields and houses they abandoned are now others'—once they return north, how can there be no contention?
translations.idiomatic: Having come south, the fields and houses they left are others'—once they return north, how can there be no contention?

sentences.zh: 切謂宜令軍戶分人歸守本業，收其晚禾，至春復還為固守計。」

translations.literal: I urgently think army households should be sent back in part to keep their original occupations, gather the late grain, and return in spring for the plan of firm defense."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that army households be sent back in part to keep their occupations, gather late grain, and return in spring for defense.

sentences.zh: 會侍御史劉元規亦言給田不便，上大悟，乃罷之。

translations.literal: Just then Attendant Censor Liu Yuangui also said giving fields was inconvenient; the emperor greatly understood and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Liu Yuangui also said giving fields was inconvenient; the emperor understood and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷同知金安軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred as vice commissioner of the Jin'an Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice commissioner of the Jin'an Army military commission.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，選為華州元帥府參議官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding he was chosen as staff officer of the Hua Prefecture commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding year two he was chosen staff officer of the Hua Prefecture commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，右都監完顏合達行帥府於楨州，嘗以前同知平涼府事卓魯回蒲乃速為參議，及移駐華州，陝西行省請復用蒲乃速，令世勣副之。

translations.literal: Earlier Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Heda ran the headquarters at Zhen Prefecture and had formerly used as staff officer Zhuolu Huipu Naisu, former vice commissioner of Pingliang; when he moved headquarters to Hua Prefecture, the Shaanxi provincial office asked to use Pu Naisu again and have Ji as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Heda ran headquarters at Zhen and had used Zhuolu Huipu Naisu, former vice commissioner of Pingliang, as staff officer; when he moved to Hua, Shaanxi asked to use Pu Naisu again with Ji as deputy.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蒲乃速但能承奉人耳，余無所長，非如世勣可任以事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Pu Naisu can only flatter others and has no other strength—not like Ji, who can be entrusted with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Pu Naisu can only flatter and has no other strength—not like Ji, who can be entrusted with affairs.

sentences.zh: 華為要鎮，而輕用其人，或致敗事。」

translations.literal: Hua is a key garrison, and to use such a man lightly may cause affairs to be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Hua is a key garrison, and to use such a man lightly may ruin affairs.

sentences.zh: 遂獨用世勣焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji alone was used.
translations.idiomatic: Ji alone was appointed.

sentences.zh: 尋入為尚書省左司郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the Ministry of Revenue as left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered Revenue as left bureau director.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，奪一官，解職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang one office was stripped and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanguang year one one office was stripped and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，世勣任華州，有薦其深通錢谷者，復察不如所舉，未籍行止中。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Ji held Hua Prefecture, someone recommended that he was deeply versed in money and grain; on re-inspection he did not match the recommendation and was not entered in the conduct register.
translations.idiomatic: While Ji held Hua Prefecture someone recommended him as deeply versed in money and grain; re-inspection did not match and he was not entered in the conduct register.

sentences.zh: 後主者舉覺，平章英王以世勣避都司之繁，私屬治籍吏冀改他職，奏下有司，故有是責。

translations.literal: Later the responsible official reported it; Grand Councilor Prince Ying, because Ji wished to avoid the tedium of the capital bureau, privately asked the conduct-register clerk hoping to change to another post—the memorial reached the authorities, and therefore came this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later the responsible official reported it; Grand Councilor Prince Ying, because Ji wished to avoid capital bureau tedium, privately asked the conduct clerk to change his post—the memorial reached the authorities and brought this punishment.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為禮部侍郎，轉司農，改太常卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised as Vice Director of Rites, transferred to Agriculture, and changed to Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After long while he was raised vice director of Rites, transferred to Agriculture, then director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 正大中，為禮部尚書，兼翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda period he was Director of Rites and concurrently Hanlin Attendant Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda he was director of Rites and concurrently Hanlin attendant expositor.

sentences.zh: 天興元年冬，哀宗將北渡，世勣率朝官劉肅、田芝等二十人求見仁安殿。

translations.literal: In the winter of Tianxing year one Emperor Aizong was about to cross north; Ji led court officers Liu Su, Tian Zhi, and twenty others to seek audience at Ren'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianxing year one Emperor Aizong was about to cross north; Ji led Liu Su, Tian Zhi, and twenty court officers to seek audience at Ren'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 上問卿等欲何言，世勣曰：「臣等聞陛下欲親出，切謂此行不便。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked what they wished to say; Ji said: "Your servants hear Your Majesty wishes to go out in person and urgently think this journey is inexpedient."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what they wished to say; Ji said: "We hear Your Majesty wishes to go out in person and urgently think the journey inexpedient.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我不出，軍分為二，一軍守，一軍出戰。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If I do not go out, the army is divided in two—one army holds, one army fights.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If I do not go out, the army is divided—one holds, one fights.

sentences.zh: 我出則軍合為一。」

translations.literal: If I go out, the army becomes one."
translations.idiomatic: If I go out, the army becomes one.

sentences.zh: 世勣曰：「陛下出則軍分為三，一守、一戰、一中軍護從，不若不出為愈也。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "If Your Majesty goes out, the army is divided in three—one holds, one fights, one central army escorts—better not to go out."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "If Your Majesty goes out, the army divides in three—one holds, one fights, one escorts—better not to go.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿等不知，我若得完顏仲德、恆山公武仙付之兵事，何勞我出。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You do not know—if I could entrust military affairs to Wanyan Zhongde and the Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian, why should I trouble to go out?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You do not know—if I could give military affairs to Wanyan Zhongde and Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian, why should I go out?

sentences.zh: 我豈不知今日將兵者，官奴統馬兵三百止矣，劉益將步兵五千止矣，欲不自將，得乎？」

translations.literal: Do I not know that those commanding troops today are only Guannu with three hundred horse at most and Liu Yi with five thousand foot at most—if I do not command myself, can it be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that today Guannu commands at most three hundred horse and Liu Yi at most five thousand foot—if I do not command myself, how can it be done?

sentences.zh: 上又指御榻曰：「我此行豈復有還期，但恨我無罪亡國耳。

translations.literal: The emperor again pointed at the imperial couch and said: "On this journey will there be a day of return—I only regret that I destroy the state without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at the imperial couch: "On this journey there will be no return—I only regret destroying the state though I am guiltless.

sentences.zh: 我未嘗奢侈，未嘗信任小人。」

translations.literal: I have never been extravagant; I have never trusted petty men."
translations.idiomatic: I have never been extravagant; I have never trusted petty men.

sentences.zh: 世勣應聲曰：「陛下用小人則亦有之。」

translations.literal: Ji answered at once: "Your Majesty has also used petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered at once: "Your Majesty has also used petty men.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「小人謂誰？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Petty men—who?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Petty men—who?"

sentences.zh: 世勣歷數曰：「移剌粘古、溫敦昌孫、兀撒惹、完顏長樂皆小人也。

translations.literal: Ji enumerated: "Yelazhangu, Wenden Changsun, Wusa Re, and Wanyan Changle are all petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Ji enumerated: "Yelazhangu, Wenden Changsun, Wusa Re, and Wanyan Changle are all petty men.

sentences.zh: 陛下不知為小人，所以用之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not know they were petty men and therefore used them."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not know they were petty men and therefore used them.

sentences.zh: 肅與世勣復多有言，良久，君臣涕泣而別。

translations.literal: Su and Ji spoke much more; after a long while emperor and ministers wept and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Ji spoke much more; after long while emperor and ministers wept and parted.

sentences.zh: 初，肅等求見，本欲數此四人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Su and the others sought audience, they had intended to enumerate these four men.
translations.idiomatic: When Su and the others sought audience they had intended to enumerate these four men.

sentences.zh: 至是，世勣獨言之，於是哀宗以世勣行。

translations.literal: At this Ji alone spoke of them, and therefore Emperor Aizong took Ji along.
translations.idiomatic: At this Ji alone named them, and Emperor Aizong took Ji along.

sentences.zh: 自蒲城至歸德。

translations.literal: From Pucheng to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: From Pucheng to Guide.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，走蔡州，次新蔡縣之姜寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the next year they fled to Cai Prefecture and halted anew at Jiang Stockade in Xincai County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the next year they fled to Cai Prefecture and halted at Jiang Stockade in Xincai County.

sentences.zh: 世勣子嵩，時為縣令，拜上于馬前，兵亂後父子始相見。

translations.literal: Ji's son Song was then county magistrate; he bowed to the emperor before his horse; only after the military turmoil did father and son first meet.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Song was then county magistrate and bowed before the emperor's horse; only after the turmoil did father and son first meet.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，授嵩應奉翰林文字，以便養親。

translations.literal: The emperor commended it and appointed Song attendant writer of the Hanlin Academy for the convenience of supporting his parent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended it and appointed Song Hanlin attendant writer so he could support his parent.

sentences.zh: 蔡城破，父子俱死。

translations.literal: When Cai city fell, father and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai city fell, father and son both died.

sentences.zh: 嵩字企隆，興定二年經義進士。

translations.literal: Song, style name Qilong, was a classics advanced scholar in the second year of Xingding.
translations.idiomatic: Song, styled Qilong, was a classics advanced scholar in Xingding year two.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：愛實言衛、鎬家屬禁錮之虐，京城括粟之暴，近侍干政之橫；

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Aishi spoke of the cruelty of imprisoning the Wei and Hao households, the violence of seizing grain in the capital, and the overbearing of inner attendants in government;
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Aishi spoke of imprisoning the Wei and Hao households, seizing grain in the capital, and inner attendants in government;

sentences.zh: 世勣言河北軍戶給田之不便，親出渡河之非計；

translations.literal: Ji spoke of the inconvenience of giving fields to Hebei army households and the ill plan of the emperor's going out in person to cross the river;
translations.idiomatic: Ji spoke of giving fields to Hebei army households and the emperor's crossing the river in person;

sentences.zh: 皆藥石之言也。

translations.literal: all were words of harsh medicine.
translations.idiomatic: all were harsh medicine.

sentences.zh: 然金至斯時，病在膏肓間矣，倉扁何施焉。

translations.literal: Yet when Jin had reached this time, the disease lay between heart and diaphragm—what could Bian Que do?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Jin had reached this hour the disease lay between heart and diaphragm—what could Bian Que do?

sentences.zh: 其為忠讜，則不可廢也。

translations.literal: As loyal remonstrance, it cannot be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: As loyal remonstrance, it cannot be discarded.
